Thank you for installing {{ .Chart.Name }}.

Your release is named {{ .Release.Name }}.

The controller and CRDs have been installed in namespace {{ .Release.Namespace }}.

To verify the installation:

  kubectl get pods -n {{ .Release.Namespace }}
  kubectl get customresourcedefinitions

To learn more about the release, try:

  $ helm status {{ .Release.Name }} -n {{ .Release.Namespace }}
  $ helm get all {{ .Release.Name }} -n {{ .Release.Namespace }}

Approval note (Manual-mode Loops, `approval.mode: Manual`):

  `cox approve <loop>` and `cox reject <loop> --reason <reason>` PATCH the
  Loop's status conditions (PlanApproved / PlanRejected) — a verb the base
  operator roles do not grant to a user. For a human to drive Manual-mode
  approvals with the `cox` CLI, install the chart with
  `rbac.helpers.enabled=true` (it creates the `loop-editor` role with
  `get;list;patch;watch` on `loops` — the verbs `cox approve`/`reject`/`diff`
  need) and bind that role to your user or group, or create an equivalent
  RoleBinding/ClusterRoleBinding yourself. Without such a binding, `cox
  approve`/`reject` are rejected by the API server (the operator still
  advances Auto-mode Loops — only Manual-mode approval needs the binding).
{{- if .Values.rbac.helpers.enabled }}

  This release installed the helper roles (rbac.helpers.enabled=true): bind
  the `loop-editor` role to a user/group to grant `cox approve`/`reject`:

    kubectl create rolebinding <name> --clusterrole loop-editor \
      --user=<user> -n {{ .Release.Namespace }}
{{- end }}
